due_when.clears_when: TWO PARTS, and the second is the one that actually protects a session. (1) The measurement is re-run and either confirms or refutes the monotonic fall-off on a later window (a second population, not the same one re-read). (2) THE CONSEQUENCE IS ABSORBED WHERE IT BITES: any clears_when clause or guard that grades a cadence against its DECLARED slot is rewritten to grade against the observed distribution, or to grade only that the cadence DELIVERED at all. ⚠️ DO NOT 'FIX' THIS BY TIGHTENING CRONS — declaring `*/30` to get hourly delivery is cargo-culting against an unverified cause and would make the shortfall worse if throttling is per-repo. ⚠️ AND IF THE OPERATOR DECIDES the sub-6-hourly cadences should move onto the VM's own timer (as the hourly digest already proposes), this does NOT clear — it CHANGES, and must be recorded as that decision with the consequence stated.
